title: A Lean file is not the Riemann prize.
friendlyTitle: A checked file is not the Riemann prize.
summary: TechCrunch reports that Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, posted an essay saying he had a Lean-compilable solution to the Riemann hypothesis, and that he asked Dario Amodei on Sunday night how to announce it. TechCrunch also reports that Stanford professor Ravi Vakil posted a separate draft of the General Riemann hypothesis by Alessandro Masullo, which Vakil said used no AI.
friendlySummary: TechCrunch reports that Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, posted an essay saying he had a solution to the Riemann hypothesis that a proof-checking program called Lean could compile. He asked Anthropic's chief executive, Dario Amodei, on Sunday night how to announce it. TechCrunch also reports that Stanford professor Ravi Vakil posted a separate draft of a related problem by Alessandro Masullo. Vakil said that draft used no AI.
whyItMatters: TechCrunch says mathematicians are still working through the Lean result, and that Alpöge has said he will pursue an explanation people can read. A file that compiles is not a Clay Mathematics Institute prize, and it is not a proof the field has accepted. Do not treat either draft as settled.
